candidates.name: Engineering Validation
candidates.hypothesis: Prioritize a reproducible engineering baseline; validate research value in real workflows.
candidates.method: Benchmark re-run + data-slice error analysis + online A/B observability design
candidates.firstExperiment: Build a minimal end-to-end pipeline first; record error distribution and explanation failure cases.
candidates.stopCondition: Narrow scope if a reproducible experimental baseline cannot be formed within two weeks.

candidates.name: Mechanism Clarification
candidates.hypothesis: Prioritize explaining "why it works" — build mechanism hypothesis with focused, strong evidence.
candidates.method: Interpretable baseline + counterfactual/causal verification + few-shot robustness test
candidates.firstExperiment: Reproduce 2 representative papers within 1 week and add interpretability metrics on public data.
candidates.stopCondition: Pause this path if two rounds of experiments fail to improve explanation consistency by >= 8%.

candidates.name: Cross-Domain Transfer
candidates.hypothesis: Transfer mature methods to new domains — pursuing higher impact while accepting higher uncertainty.
candidates.method: Cross-domain data adaptation + transfer learning + error attribution & failure boundary analysis
candidates.firstExperiment: Verify cross-domain transfer with minimum sample settings; check for significant negative transfer.
candidates.stopCondition: Fall back to P1 or P2 if negative transfer persists > 2 iterations with no interpretability improvement.

tiers.label: High-credibility Academic Source
tiers.rule: Journals / top conferences / official databases; prioritized as basis for conclusions

tiers.label: Medium-credibility Frontier Source
tiers.rule: Preprints / conference reports; usable for frontier hypotheses, not as sole decision basis

tiers.label: Low-credibility Supplementary Source
tiers.rule: Blogs / whitepapers / community posts; background only, not core evidence

conflictRules: Same-tier conflict: mark as unresolved; require human confirmation before convergence.
Cross-tier conflict: default to higher-tier evidence unless lower tier has newer data and reproducible results.
If conflict directly impacts topic conclusion, the system forces a falsifiable experiment instead of deciding outright.
Any conclusion without citations is excluded from candidate path scoring.
